blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Supply chain KPIs are only useful if three things are true: the numbers are clean, the review rhythm is regular, and the decisions are actually made from them. A beautiful dashboard that nobody trusts, or that is only looked at in a crisis, is worse than no dashboard at all — it gives the illusion of visibility without the discipline.

Mature teams are ruthless about data quality. They fix calculation errors quickly. They agree, clearly, what each KPI measures and what it does not. And they review the core handful — OTIF, fill rate, inventory turnover, on-time-to-promise — every week, with the same small group of people, making the same small number of decisions.

Over a year, this quiet rhythm produces the kind of operational stability that looks effortless to outsiders. It is not. It is the product of a very disciplined weekly hour.

items.q: According to the text, three things must be true for KPIs to be useful. Which is one of them?
options: The KPIs must be reviewed only in a crisis
The review rhythm must be regular
The dashboard must be visually beautiful
The metrics must be tracked daily
items.why: "the numbers are clean, the review rhythm is regular, and the decisions are actually made from them."

items.q: Why is a dashboard nobody trusts described as "worse than no dashboard at all"?
options: It is only updated once a year
It gives the illusion of visibility without the discipline
It is too complex for outsiders
items.why: "it gives the illusion of visibility without the discipline."

items.q: What does the author suggest by saying mature teams review "with the same small group of people, making the same small number of decisions"?
options: Consistency of people and decisions is part of the discipline
Only senior leaders should attend the review
The review should change format every week
items.why: Inferência: repetir as mesmas pessoas e o mesmo foco é justamente o que cria o ritmo disciplinado.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A polished dashboard is enough to prove a team is in control
Each KPI needs a clear definition
A regular rhythm can produce stability over time
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que a beleza do painel não vale nada sem confiança e disciplina.

items.q: What does the ending — "It is not. It is the product of a very disciplined weekly hour" — imply about operational stability?
options: It looks easy but is built by sustained discipline
It can only be achieved over several years
items.why: Inferência: parece "effortless" de fora, mas é fruto de trabalho disciplinado toda semana.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry falando ao time sobre o painel de KPIs. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me be honest with you about this dashboard. For the last three months, two of our numbers — fill rate and OTIF — were calculated in two different ways, depending on who built the report. So when the board looked at the slide, they were comparing figures that never meant the same thing.

That is why nobody in operations trusts it anymore. And I don't blame them. A number you can't rely on is worse than no number at all.

So here is what we're going to do. Before the next review, I want one agreed definition for each KPI, written down, signed off, no exceptions. If two calculations disagree, we fix the calculation first — we do not argue about it in the meeting.

Then we go back to a weekly rhythm. Same hour, same small group, the core handful only: OTIF, fill rate, inventory turnover, on-time-to-promise. The data may suggest a problem, or indicate a trend, but the decision is ours to make, and we make it there and then.

Give me one disciplined hour a week, and in a year this will look effortless. It won't be. But it will work.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What went wrong with the dashboard over the last three months?
options: The board refused to look at the slides
Fill rate and OTIF were calculated in two different ways
The team stopped updating the numbers
items.why: "two of our numbers — fill rate and OTIF — were calculated in two different ways."

items.q: What is Harry's first fix before the next review?
options: Add more KPIs to the dashboard
One agreed, written definition for each KPI
Move the meeting to a bigger room
items.why: "I want one agreed definition for each KPI, written down, signed off, no exceptions."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "we fix the calculation first — we do not argue about it in the meeting"?
options: The meeting should be cancelled if numbers disagree
Arguments are banned from all meetings
Only Harry decides which calculation is correct
Data disputes should be resolved before the review, not during it
items.why: Inferência: a reunião é para decidir, não para debater qual número está certo — isso se resolve antes.

items.q: Why does Harry say the result "won't be" effortless, even though it will look that way?
options: Because the appearance of ease hides the weekly discipline behind it
Because the board keeps changing the targets
Because the team is too small to cope
items.why: Inferência: o "effortless" é a aparência externa; por dentro há uma hora disciplinada toda semana.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's tone?
options: Honest about the failure but firm about the fix
items.why: Inferência: ele admite o problema com franqueza, mas propõe um plano claro e exige disciplina.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We won't report anything until the data is clean." Here, clean data means data that is…
items.why: Clean data = dados limpos, sem erros nem inconsistências.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A steady weekly ___ turns raw numbers into consistent decisions."
items.why: Review rhythm = ritmo de revisão, a cadência regular que gera as decisões.

items.q: "The report was polished, but it gave a false illusion of control." An illusion is…
options: a misleading impression that is not real
items.why: Illusion = ilusão, uma impressão enganosa que não corresponde à realidade.

items.q: "Good teams are ruthless about data quality." Being ruthless here means being…
items.why: Ruthless = implacável; aqui, rigoroso e sem concessões com a qualidade dos dados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "From the outside the operation looked ___, but inside it took real discipline."
items.why: Effortless = sem esforço; a estabilidade parece fácil de fora, mas exige disciplina por dentro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de revisão de KPIs. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new KPI definitions." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the corrected dashboard team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two analysts pushed back on the new fill-rate formula." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar, questionar.

items.q: "The team agreed to clean the data but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "A prettier chart won't move the needle on trust." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não muda nada de fato.
